findings.title: WatchdogTest AC-6 and AC-4 assert JVM-global scheduler state in the shared test JVM and fail when any other test leaves a reservation pending
findings.description: NaruServe-proxy tests run in one JVM (no forkEvery for this module) and ProxyExchange.Scheduler.INSTANCE is a JVM-wide singleton. awaitQueued(0) in AC-6 compares the absolute queue size with 0, and AC-4 requires that no thread named naruserve-proxy*watchdog* is alive at all within 30 s. Any reservation left by another test class (an in-flight request under the default 5-minute total timeout, a ProxyExchange never released) makes AC-6 fail with 'expected:<0> but was:<1>' and keeps the watchdog thread alive so AC-4 fails too. The tests currently pass only because of the class execution order and the absence of a leak elsewhere; they are order-dependent and not hermetic.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC-6 take a baseline queuedReservations() before the 1000 requests and assert the queue returns to that baseline (and baseline+>=1 while the held request is in flight). Run the AC-4 idle-thread check in a fresh JVM like the AC-1/AC-5 LazyProbe (or move WatchdogTest to a forkEvery=1 isolated task as NaruServe-tinyhttpd does for *IsolatedSocketTest).
